uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of how fast prices paid by UK households are rising. It is the figure the Bank of England's 2% target is set against, and it feeds into benefit, pension and rail-fare upratings.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The September reading arrives as economists warn that UK inflation would reach 5% if a US diesel ban goes ahead, a reminder of how directly fuel costs pass into British prices. The release sets the baseline that warning is measured from: where prices stood before any such shock.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the federal funds rate. Its decisions reprice US mortgages and loans, and dollar debt owed by governments and firms worldwide.
fomc-2026-10.recent: Minutes of the September meeting show most officials expecting another hike by year-end but split on why: an oil shock lifts prices and slows the economy at once. Since then the Labor Department counted 29,000 new jobs against 90,000 expected, setting stalled hiring against inflation that has run above target for five and a half years.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council meets roughly every six weeks to set interest rates for the countries that share the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, and Lagarde has painted a darkening picture on prices while business activity runs at a 3½-year high. The Governing Council meets with France's bond market under stress, and Moulin has said the ECB is not there to deal with the fiscal problems of countries.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and one of the world's largest government bond markets, and borrowing costs well beyond Japan.
boj-2026-10.recent: Three sources say the bank is weighing a declaration that underlying inflation has hit its 2% goal, the judgment its whole case for higher rates rests on. Japanese yields jumped as a global bond sell-off deepened, and this meeting settles whether the bank puts that judgment on the record.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. That rate feeds through to British mortgages, business loans and savings, and sterling moves on the vote.
boe-2026-11.recent: The committee votes while its largest peers lean toward tightening: most Federal Reserve officials expect another rate hike by year-end, and a surprise inflation jump across the euro zone has put pressure on the ECB. The decision settles whether the Bank of England moves with them or holds apart.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the Federal Reserve's rate-setting body, meets eight times a year to set the federal funds rate. Its decisions move borrowing costs in the US and reprice dollar debt worldwide.
fomc-2026-12.recent: Minutes of the September meeting show most officials expecting to raise rates but divided over the logic: the oil shock they are tightening into lifts prices and slows the economy at once. A month that added 29,000 jobs sharpens that split, and Warsh has held his focus on price stability with inflation above target for five and a half years.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of the leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by a rotating presidency. Its members account for about 85% of global output, and its communiqués set the direction for trade, debt and financial rules.
g20-2026-miami.recent: Trump has invited Putin to the Miami G20, an invitation Rubio confirmed and the Kremlin put on its briefing agenda, so attendance itself is at stake. The summit follows a Trump-Xi meeting that ended with a US-China AI communication channel, and arrives with a US-India trade deal that Greer says is not imminent.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council sets interest rates for the countries that share the euro, meeting about every six weeks. Its decisions set borrowing costs for some 350 million people and move the euro.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September while business activity ran at a 3½-year high, and Lagarde has painted a darkening picture of prices. Against that sits France, whose bond market is under strain: Moulin said the conditions for intervention are not met. The Governing Council sets one rate for both.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's nine-member Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its vote reaches mortgage and business loan costs across Britain, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: The meeting falls after a turn toward tightening among the committee's peers: most Federal Reserve officials expect another rate hike by year-end, and a surprise inflation jump across the euro zone has put pressure on the ECB. It settles whether the Bank of England's rate follows them or holds apart.

boj-2026-12.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yields on the largest government debt, relative to its economy, of any rich country.
boj-2026-12.recent: Three sources say the Bank of Japan may declare underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal, the condition it has set for years before raising rates further. Japanese yields jumped as a global bond sell-off deepened. This meeting decides what the bank does once its own test is passed.

fred-us-cpi-2026-10-14.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what urban households pay for goods and services. Treasury yields, the dollar and Social Security adjustments all move with it.
fred-us-cpi-2026-10-14.recent: Most Federal Reserve officials expect another rate hike by year-end, yet the Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected. This print is the inflation half of that split: it shows whether prices are rising fast enough to justify tightening into a stalled hiring market.

fred-us-ppi-2026-10-15.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of the prices US producers receive for goods and services. It shows cost pressure before it reaches shop shelves, and feeds the inflation gauge the Federal Reserve targets.
fred-us-ppi-2026-10-15.recent: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reports the prices producers received last month. The release settles whether cost pressure at the factory gate and in wholesale services is building or easing before it reaches consumers.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-10-15.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly estimate of what American shops, restaurants and online sellers took in. Consumer spending is about two-thirds of the US economy, so it moves growth forecasts, Treasury yields and the dollar.
fred-us-retail-sales-2026-10-15.recent: The Census Bureau reports its first estimate of last month's US retail sales, with revisions to the months before it. The release settles whether household spending held up or slowed, the largest single input to the quarter's growth figure.
